clue.text: Dope found in most unlikely area of jungle

indicators.note: found in says one piece sits inside the other in this clue

parts.note: most unlikely means rarest
dope is slang for information, info

explanation.surface: Somebody has stumbled on drugs in the remotest corner of a jungle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' looks like drugs but here it is slang for inside information.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical forest with heavy rainfall is the typical jungle habitat.

clue.text: State support raised for star

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a leg is a support, as under a table

explanation.surface: A government's backing has been increased, making it a star.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigel is a bright star in the constellation Orion.

clue.text: Rhetorician is found round soapboxes, say

parts.note: round means the letter O, which is round in shape
soapboxes are an example of crates, used as platforms for speakers

explanation.surface: A public speaker is spotted standing on soapboxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Isocrates was an ancient Athenian teacher of oratory.

clue.text: Find me in engine, as arranged — that avoids stress at the end of the line

definitions.text: that avoids stress at the end of the line

indicators.note: as arranged says the preceding words are to be set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is told to look for them inside a motor, apparently while writing poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: In verse, a line closing on an unstressed extra syllable has this ending, so the final beat is soft.

clue.text: Despicable people, supporters of Napoleon, guillotined

indicators.note: guillotined means beheaded, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: Napoleon is the pig in Orwell's Animal Farm, and a pig's feet are trotters

explanation.surface: French revolutionaries executed the vile backers of the emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to the French emperor, but this Napoleon is Orwell's pig, standing on trotters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotters is dated British slang for scoundrels or cads.

clue.text: Bulb revealed everything in photograph

indicators.note: in places one word inside another here

parts.note: a shot is a photograph
all means everything

explanation.surface: A light bulb shows up the whole scene in a snapshot.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallot is a small onion-like vegetable grown from a bulb.

clue.text: Song missing second prize

indicators.note: missing says a letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: a psalm is a sacred song

explanation.surface: A singer who came second missed out on the award.
explanation.definitionFit: The palm, a branch of the tree, was awarded as a symbol of victory, so it means a prize.

clue.text: Excellent part of Bible for Irish missionary

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as the letters A and I
Daniel, abbreviated Dan, is a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A fine passage of Scripture is chosen for a preacher from Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Aidan was an Irish monk who founded the community on Lindisfarne.

clue.text: Plant in second city where all the men work to rule

definitions.text: where all the men work to rule

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: in says one piece is set inside the other here

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York, a city
an aster is a flowering plant

explanation.surface: A factory in Britain's second city has staff staging a work-to-rule protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work to rule' suggests industrial action, but monks work under a monastic rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks live and labour in their house under a religious order's rule.

clue.text: Interpretation of sacred music — work in large volume

definitions.meaning: a staging or performance of a setting of the Mass is a production of it
manufacture of goods in huge quantities

explanation.definitionFit: Factory output on a huge scale is called this, and a performance of a Mass setting reads the same way.

clue.text: German general not quite inside great protective ring

indicators.note: inside says the trimmed name sits within the other piece

parts.note: GT is an abbreviation for great

indicators.note: not quite means the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Rommel was a German field marshal of the Second World War

explanation.surface: A German commander is nearly surrounded by a big defensive circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A grommet is a ring, often metal or rubber, protecting the edge of a hole.

clue.text: A youth with ring given no end of rubbing?

definitions.text: A youth with ring given no end of rubbing?

parts.note: a lad is a youth
a din is a loud ringing noise

explanation.surface: A young fellow owning a ring keeps polishing it endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the pantomime hero, who rubbed his ring and lamp to summon genies.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Arabian Nights tale, the lad summons a genie by rubbing a magic ring and lamp.

clue.text: An allergy developed in the throat

indicators.note: developed says the letters have been worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone's hay fever has spread to their neck.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective refers to the voice box, an organ located in the neck.

clue.text: Empty place head has is rejected by student body

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students, a British student organisation

explanation.surface: A vacant spot at the top of a college is turned down by the students' union.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinus is an air-filled cavity in the skull.

clue.text: Some drop a tenner in the plate at church

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A churchgoer puts a ten-pound note in the collection plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A paten is the small dish holding the bread at Communion.

clue.text: Making a minimal distance in headway, ship abandoned timetable

indicators.note: in places the two pieces inside the shortened word
abandoned says those letters are left out of the word

parts.note: progress means headway
SS stands for steamship
mm, a millimetre, is a tiny distance

explanation.surface: A ship making little progress gave up its sailing schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' removes SS from PROGRESS, leaving PROGRE, into which A and MM go.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme is a schedule or plan of events.

clue.text: Dark, so go to bed in cover freely supplied

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other here

parts.note: an SAE, stamped addressed envelope, is a cover sent with postage paid
to turn in is to go to bed

explanation.surface: It is late, so someone heads to bed under free blankets.
explanation.walkthrough: An SAE is enclosed so a reply costs the recipient nothing: a British convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine means gloomy or sombre in temperament.

clue.text: Ruined volume needs fresh cover

indicators.note: cover says the one word wraps round the letter

parts.note: fresh in the sense of cheeky means insolent

explanation.surface: A damaged book has to be given a new jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' looks like new but means cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone financially ruined cannot pay their debts.

clue.text: Part of main base needed for the rest of the natives?

definitions.text: Part of main base needed for the rest of the natives?

parts.words: Part of main base needed for the rest of the natives?
parts.note: the main is the sea, natives are oysters raised there, and they need a place on the seabed to rest

explanation.definitionFit: Native oysters are cultivated on a seabed patch, which serves as their resting place.

clue.text: Bill's victim falls near here

definitions.meaning: ... Bill Cody killed thousands of bison
the US city lies close to Niagara Falls

explanation.definitionFit: The bison hunted by Buffalo Bill share the name of the New York city near Niagara.

clue.text: Medical man inspiring respect for art

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
awing means filling with awe or respect

explanation.surface: A doctor commands admiration for his paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: Sketching with pencil or pen is a form of visual art.

clue.text: Study composition of little interest

indicators.note: composition says the letters are put together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A piece of academic work is rather boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dusty is dry and dull.

clue.text: Appropriately dressed in a way to receive honour?

indicators.note: to receive says the first word takes the second inside it

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is an honour

explanation.surface: Someone wears suitable attire to collect an award.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British honour given by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Robed means wearing ceremonial gowns, suitable dress for an occasion.

clue.text: False, treacherous place — no good

parts.note: a bog is marshy, dangerous ground
US, unserviceable, is slang for useless

explanation.surface: A deceptive marsh is good for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogus means fake or counterfeit.

clue.text: In general, duck going over — or partridge

parts.note: Franco was the Spanish general and dictator

indicators.note: going over means turned round, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing, nil, in cricket

explanation.surface: A commander watches a duck or a partridge fly over.
explanation.definitionFit: The francolin is an African and Asian game bird related to the partridge.

clue.text: Three elements of an organ

parts.note: Na is the symbol for sodium
S is the symbol for sulphur
Al is the symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: Three parts make up an instrument with pipes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests the instrument, but it is the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasal relates to the nose, an organ of smell.

clue.text: Many a spy captured in battle

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, hence many
an agent is a spy

explanation.surface: Lots of spies are taken prisoner during a war.
explanation.definitionFit: Magenta, in Italy, was the site of an 1859 battle between France and Austria.

clue.text: Greenland's nature reserve

definitions.meaning: the cold frozen quality of an Arctic land

explanation.definitionFit: Frostiness describes Arctic cold and also a chilly, distant manner.

clue.text: Boy from Rugby going thus to Cambridge

definitions.meaning: a schoolboy friend of the hero in Tom Brown's Schooldays, set at Rugby School
Cambridge lies in this compass direction from Rugby

explanation.walkthrough: Rugby is an English public school and town in the Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: The point of the compass from Rugby towards Cambridge also names Tom Brown's schoolfriend.

clue.text: Complete return of schoolwork, perhaps, after taking leave

indicators.note: after taking puts the reversed piece behind the other

parts.note: a conge is formal permission to leave

indicators.note: return of means the word is turned back

parts.note: Latin is an example of a school subject

explanation.surface: A pupil hands in all their homework before going on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Congenital, as in a congenital liar, means utter or thorough.
